title: Binary tree upside down
md:
## The idea

Only the **left spine** moves. Walking down it, each node takes its old **right sibling** as its new left child and its old **parent** as its new right child. Keep three references while walking, exactly like reversing a linked list.

## Step by step

1. cur = root, parent = null, parentRight = null.
2. Save nextLeft = cur.Left.
3. cur.Left = parentRight; parentRight = cur.Right; cur.Right = parent.
4. parent = cur; cur = nextLeft. Repeat.
5. Return parent — the old leftmost node.

## Worked example

**Input:** tree [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| at 1 | left = null, right = null; remember 3 |
| at 2 | left = 3, right = 1; remember 5 |
| at 4 | left = 5, right = 2 |
| done | new root 4 |

**Result:** [4, 5, 2, null, null, 3, 1]

## Cost

O(h) time, O(1) extra memory.

## The code (C#, compiled and tested against every part of the question)

```csharp
// TreeNode is provided by the starter (Models.cs): int Value; TreeNode Left, Right.

// LeetCode 156 — turn the tree upside down. Every right node is a leaf with a left sibling, or missing.
// The leftmost node becomes the root; each node's old parent becomes its right child,
// and the old right sibling becomes its left child.
public static class UpsideDown {
    public static TreeNode Flip(TreeNode root) {
        TreeNode cur = root, parent = null, parentRight = null;
        while (cur != null) {                  // walk down the left spine
            TreeNode nextLeft = cur.Left;      // remember where to go before rewiring
            cur.Left = parentRight;            // old sibling becomes the left child
            parentRight = cur.Right;           // this node's right child is the sibling for the next one
            cur.Right = parent;                // old parent becomes the right child
            parent = cur;
            cur = nextLeft;
        }
        return parent;                         // the last node visited: the old leftmost leaf
    }
}
```

## Likely follow-up questions

**Q: Why does the shape guarantee matter?**

It means right nodes never have children, so they can always become left leaves.

**Q: Complexity?**

O(h) time, O(1) extra iteratively; O(h) stack recursively.

**Q: Shared state?**

It rewires the caller's tree — nobody else may read it during the flip.

**Q: Keep the original?**

Copy the spine first, or build new nodes while walking.

**Q: Related?**

Reverse a linked list — exactly the same pointer dance.
